newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS-DeTeMobil Czech venture posts losses.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-DeTeMobil Czech venture posts losses.

text.p: RadioMobil a.s., a Czech mobile telephone joint venture managed by a unit of Deutsche Telekom AG, said on Tuesday that it would post large losses after heavy investment in the startup of its GSM digital network.
Gustav Hraska, RadioMobil's financial director, told a news conference that the company had a 839 million crown loss for 1996, and expected a 900 million crown loss this year.
But he said that the GSM network, called Paegas, should begin to show a profit next year.
"Already by 1998 we can be back into black numbers," Hraska said.
Radiomobil said its investment had been entirely self-financed in 1996 with two billion crowns ploughed in last year and another 5.3 billion crowns expected in 1997.
Hraska said RadioMobil would soon announce a manadate for an investment bank to arrange a 300 million mark syndicated loan to further its development.

RadioMobil, which operates one of two Czech GSM digital networks, is comprised 51 percent of Czech transmission company Ceske Radiokomunikace a.s. and 49 percent of an international consortium led by Deutsche Telekom's mobile telephone unit DeTeMobil.

The consortium, C Mobil, won a government tender for the GSM licence last year over several international groups, promising investment of roughly $200 million by mid-1997, and aiming to take quickly more than 50 percent of market share.
DeTeMobil holds an 84.55 percent of the consortium's interest in RadioMobil and has assumed the top management positions of the venture.
Italy's STET International holds 12 percent in C Mobil.
RadioMobil is in direct competition with Eurotel s.r.o., a joint venture of Czech SPT Telecom a.s., and an American consortium comprised of U.S. West Media Group and Bell Atlantic Corp.
RadioMobil said on Tuesday that its Paegas service, which was launched in September last year, had over 70,000 clients and the network covered 80 percent of the Czech population.

In April, Eurotel reported having about 140,000 clients on its GSM network, which was launched about three months before Paegas. In all Eurotel said its client base had topped 200,000 when users of its older analogue NMT service were included.
In a statement, RadioMobil blamed a slow rollout of the network in the intial stage on bureaucracy.

"After initial problems, which appeared at the beginning of construction of the Paegas network and were caused mainly by buearacratic obstacles Radiomobil... was able to fulfil expectations made a year ago," it said.
